title: A bishop’s fourth-century church, rebuilt in Romanesque brick
episode: An ancient sacred space in modern Milan, Sant'Ambrogio
description: Ambrose, bishop of Milan, founded this basilica in the 380s and lies in its crypt. Smarthistory looks at the Basilica of Sant’Ambrogio, whose brick Romanesque church and arcaded forecourt date mostly from the 11th and 12th centuries.

title: Leonardo applies for a job and barely mentions painting
episode: Letter to the Duke of Milan
description: Around 1482 Leonardo da Vinci wrote to Ludovico Sforza, ruler of Milan, offering bridges, cannon and siege engines, with painting near the end. The draft survives in the Codex Atlanticus, kept at the Biblioteca Ambrosiana library.

title: A Last Supper painted on a monks’ dining-room wall
description: Leonardo painted the Last Supper around 1495–98 in the refectory of the Dominican convent at Santa Maria delle Grazie church. His experimental paint mix began flaking within his lifetime; Smarthistory looks at what survives.

title: A dead Christ seen feet-first
episode: Andrea Mantegna, Lamentation over the Dead Christ, c. 1483
description: Andrea Mantegna’s Lamentation over the Dead Christ, around 1483, shows the body from the feet in steep foreshortening, mourners squeezed at the edge. It hangs in the Pinacoteca di Brera, the gallery in a former Jesuit college.

title: A young Raphael reworks his teacher’s wedding scene
description: Raphael was about 21 when he painted the Marriage of the Virgin in 1504 for a church in Città di Castello, reworking a design by his teacher Perugino. It entered the Pinacoteca di Brera art gallery in 1806.

title: A duke kneels in armour under a hanging ostrich egg
episode: Piero della Francesca, Madonna and Child with Saints, Angels, and Federico da  Montefeltro
description: Piero della Francesca’s altarpiece shows Federico da Montefeltro, Duke of Urbino, kneeling in armour before the Virgin, an ostrich egg hanging from the shell-shaped apse. It came from Urbino to the Pinacoteca di Brera gallery in 1811.

title: Venetian merchants search Alexandria’s tombs for a saint
episode: Tintoretto, The Finding of the Body of Saint Mark
description: Jacopo Tintoretto painted the Finding of the Body of Saint Mark in the 1560s for a Venetian confraternity, with men pulling corpses from tombs in Alexandria down a deep vaulted hall. It now hangs in Milan’s Pinacoteca di Brera gallery.

place: Museo del Novecento, Piazza del Duomo
title: Painters in love with speed, machines and the modern city
description: Poet Filippo Tommaso Marinetti launched Futurism in 1909, and its painters, led by Umberto Boccioni, worked in Milan, celebrating speed, machines and war. The Museo del Novecento, the 20th-century art museum on Piazza del Duomo, holds key works.

title: Walking among the spires on the cathedral roof
episode: To God, from the Rooftop of Milan’s Cathedral
description: Rick Steves climbs onto the marble roof terraces of the Duomo, Milan’s Gothic cathedral, begun in 1386 and worked on for nearly six centuries, where visitors walk among its forest of spires and statues.

place: Piazza Affari, outside the stock exchange
title: A marble middle finger faces the stock exchange
description: Artist Maurizio Cattelan’s marble hand, L.O.V.E., with every finger cut off but the middle one, has stood since 2010 in Piazza Affari square, facing the 1930s stock exchange. Rick Steves considers who it is meant for.

title: Glass towers and tree-covered flats on old railway land
episode: The New Milan at Porta Nuova
description: Rick Steves visits Porta Nuova, a business district built on former rail yards in the 2010s, with the spired UniCredit Tower above Piazza Gae Aulenti square and Stefano Boeri’s planted apartment towers, the Bosco Verticale (Vertical Forest).

title: The city’s uprising against Austria, told in a quiet museum
episode: Milan’s Risorgimento Museum: Now Free…and Still Empty
description: The Risorgimento was the 19th-century drive to unify Italy, and Milan’s Five Days revolt against Austrian rule in March 1848 was a turning point. Rick Steves visits the Risorgimento Museum in Palazzo Moriggia, a mansion in Brera.

title: Domed concrete igloo homes from the postwar housing crisis
description: In 1946 engineer Mario Cavallè built a small estate of domed concrete houses in the Maggiolina neighbourhood as quick postwar housing. The Tim Traveller visits the survivors, on and around Via Lepanto, still lived in today.

title: A world’s fair about feeding the planet
description: Milan hosted the 2015 World Expo, themed “Feeding the Planet, Energy for Life”, on a new site at Rho on the city’s northwest edge. DW’s lifestyle show Euromaxx tours the national pavilions; the grounds are now the MIND science district.
